title: UNHCR asylum corridor application doubling
summary: Research task: at the publication of year-D complete annual asylum statistics (an HDX refresh observed in D+1), from corridor features that read only published years up to D, predict whether an asylum corridor (origin x host) with at least 500 government-procedure applications in year D doubles to at least twice that value in year D+1. Annual grain, label years 2002-2025, 7,212 eligible corridor-years across fixed disjoint temporal splits. A publication-lag nowcast explicitly labelled as retrospective research under a restricted protocol - not an enforced benchmark and not an operational forecast.

post.title: Will an asylum corridor double next year? A frozen annual panel, honestly framed
paragraphs: UNHCR publishes annual asylum applications by corridor (country of origin x country of asylum) as an open CSV on the Humanitarian Data Exchange, refreshed in place and carrying no historical vintages. The contribution here is not access: it is the sha256-pinned source snapshot, the derived doubling label, the eligibility frame (at least 500 government-procedure applications in year D and a published year-D-1 corridor value), fixed disjoint temporal splits, and a scored contract. 7,212 eligible corridor-years: train label years 2002-2016 (3,363 rows, 283 positives), eval 2017-2021 (1,887 rows, 165), and a labeled holdout 2022-2025 (1,962 rows, 227) that ships but is never scored in development.

The packaged baseline is illustrative, and the comparisons decide what the number means. The stock runner-contract baseline reaches eval AUC 0.5393 (Brier 0.0851) on the 1,887 eval rows, while on identical rows a persistence-momentum reference reaches 0.5742 and a persistence surge flag 0.5856; a calendar/identity control reaches 0.5409. Every paired dependence-aware 95% interval for the model-versus-reference differences contains zero. Headroom above persistence is therefore not demonstrated by the packaged evidence; the negative finding is recorded beside the number, and both are quoted together or not at all.

Before publication an independent adversarial audit (2026-10-28) returned DO NOT PUBLISH: the shipped illustrative validator passes the whole eval feature table to the predictor, so the package's earlier claim of an enforced isolated-rows protocol was unenforced at runtime. The auditor's frozen label-blind attacks recovered eval AUC 0.9753 from eval features alone, 0.9830 from holdout features, 0.9970 across all splits, and exact label counts. The operator directed honest re-description rather than enforcement claims: the corrected package states isolated rows as a requirement, quotes those measured recoveries, corrects the exclusion counts (377 missing-history corridor-years), documents target_date as a calendar identifier, and declares all 14 runner inputs. The corrected artifact was re-qualified through gate 1.5.0 over the exact accepted bytes, and publication is additionally gated on an independent re-audit of the corrected package. No enforced-protocol claim is made, and scores produced under unrestricted table access are meaningless.

This is a publication-lag nowcast, not a future-event forecast. The prediction instant is the HDX refresh carrying complete year-D data (the observed 2026-08-20 resource carries complete data through 2025); every feature reads published years up to D, while the target year's value is entirely unpublished on that channel at the instant even though the target year has partially elapsed. Because the archive is revised in place, all rows are construction-time vintage over the pinned snapshot - no point-in-time reconstruction is claimed. Cross-row outcome exposure is measured and recorded (a next-year copy of the corridor's own surge feature), so the dataset serves retrospective model-development research under a restricted protocol, and no operational forecasting claim is made.

limitations: Derived research dataset, not an official UNHCR product; UNHCR has not reviewed, authorised or endorsed it.

Retrospective research under a restricted isolated-rows protocol that the shipped illustrative runner does NOT enforce: the validator passes the whole eval table to the predictor, and the independent audit measured label-blind recoveries (eval AUC 0.975325, holdout 0.983034, 0.996970 across all splits, exact count recovery). Scores under unrestricted access are meaningless.
A publication-lag nowcast, not a future-event forecast: the target year has partially elapsed at the prediction instant, and its value is unpublished on the channel at that instant.

Current-vintage archive: HDX distributes one revised-in-place resource with no historical vintages, so values are construction-time vintage over the sha256-pinned source (fetched 2026-10-27); no as-of availability ledger exists.
Annual grain only: the machine-fetchable extract has no month column, and the publisher's monthly grain stays behind its interactive application, so no monthly variant is buildable from this channel.

Government-procedure stream only: the task sums G/P rows; corridors served only by UNHCR-run procedures are outside the task, and temporary-protection registrations (for example Ukrainians in the EU from 2022) are not asylum applications and do not enter this stream.
Eligibility requires a published year-D-1 corridor value; 377 otherwise-eligible corridor-years (314 train / 31 eval / 32 holdout) are excluded for missing history.
Host-silent censoring: 33 corridor-years whose host reports no rows at all in D+1 are excluded as unobserved targets, never counted as zero, and censoring never decides another row's membership.

Duplicate-row resolution is a construction rule, not a publisher-documented split: 28.5% of corridor-year cells carry multiple rows summed per corridor-year, cross-checked against the publisher's own host-year totals (BAMF Germany, within 0.005-0.09% across four years).
Prevalence drift across splits (train 8.4%, eval 8.7%, holdout 11.6%): the holdout is prevalence-shifted relative to training - a property of the period, reported rather than hidden.
Positives cluster by (origin, label-year) surge events beyond the row grain: 109 distinct positive clusters in eval and 133 in holdout; per-label-year positive counts are reported beside every score.

The illustrative stock baseline trails both persistence references on identical eval rows (0.5393 vs 0.5742 momentum and 0.5856 surge flag; every paired 95% interval contains zero); headroom above persistence is not demonstrated.

Cross-row outcome exposure is measured and recorded (a 12-months-later copy of the corridor's own surge feature is present for many corridors); honest evaluation requires isolated rows and an enforced restricted protocol.
The labeled holdout is downloadable by design; keep it and its labels outside every evaluated agent's workspace.

Source data is the publisher's own distribution under CC BY 3.0 IGO (attribution required, no implied endorsement, changes must be labelled); our compilation contribution is dedicated CC0-1.0 and the code is MIT.
